html:
Kurmanjan Datka was a Kyrgyz leader of the Alay mountains in the south of Kyrgyzstan, known as the Queen of the South. She was born in 1811 and died in 1907.

She left an arranged marriage, which was rare and shocking, and later married Alymbek, a chief who served the Khanate of Kokand. After he was killed in 1862 she led his tribes herself, and the khan and the emir of Bukhara gave her the title of datka, general.

When the Russian Empire took Kokand in 1876, she judged resistance hopeless and agreed to accept Russian rule, keeping her people from being wiped out. One of her sons was later hanged by the Russians for smuggling, and she did not plead for him. Today she is a national heroine of Kyrgyzstan: on the banknotes, and the subject of a 2014 film.
